4031.name: Front left wheel speed sensor
4031.desc: The speed signal of the indicated wheel is missing or wrong.  Check:  - the wheel sensor and the associated wiring to the ABS ECU for opens, shorts and weak connections, and the ECU for proper ground.  - the sensor continuity and resistance  - the ECU ground connection  - the air gap between sensor and impulse ring  - the impulse ring and sensor to have no signs of damage or deformation, and to be free of magnetic dust  - the wheel bearing for excessive play  NOTE:  - It is ESSENTIAL that all the rims and tires are of the same size, as specified by the manufacturer, and that the tires have correct pressure and show uniform wear  - using an Oscilloscope to check the signal gives an excellent visual reference of the signal integrity and enables easy comparison between the wheel sensors.  - this code may be set if a wheel is rotated independently when the car is lifted up and the Key is ON.

0133.name: Lambda 1 signal above catalyser
0133.desc: The Signal of the Lambda Sensor after the catalytic converter indicated by the code is missing or out of the range. The after-cat Lambda Sensor signals the Oxygen status of the exhaust gases after the NOx reduction and CO and HC oxidation reactions in the converter, and enables the ECU to monitor the converter efficiency.  Before replacing the sensor, check:  - The Lambda level of the exhaust gases with an emissions analyzer.  - Any possibilities for stray air to get drawn into the system between the pre- and after-cat Lambda sensors, like a leak in the exhaust system or in the Secondary Air system (if installed).  - The status of the after-cat Lambda Sensor when the system is in operating temperature. Increase the RPM to 2000 for 20 sec, then snap the throttle 2-3 times. The signal should change status briskly. If not, check the sensor and wiring.  NOTE: Depending on the system, Lambda sensors with voltage range of 0-5V or 0-1V may be used.

013A.name: Lambda 1 signal below catalyser
013A.desc: The Signal of the Lambda Sensor after the catalytic converter indicated by the code is missing or out of the range. Before replacing the sensor, check:  - The Lambda level of the exhaust gases with an emissions analyzer.  - Any possibilities for stray air to get drawn into the system between the pre- and after-cat Lambda sensors, like a leak in the exhaust system or in the Secondary Air system (if installed).  - The status of the after-cat Lambda Sensor when the system is in operating temperature. Increase the RPM to 2000 for 20 sec, then snap the throttle 2-3 times. The signal should change status briskly. If not, check the sensor and wiring.  NOTE: Depending on the system, Lambda sensors with voltage range of 0-5V or 0-1V may be used.

The after-cat Lambda Sensor signals the Oxygen status of the exhaust gases after the NOx reduction and CO and HC oxidation reactions in the converter, and enables the ECU to monitor the converter efficiency.
